# simdutf / base64

simdutf's own fuzz target `base64` ([source](source/base64.cpp), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over simdutf (simdutf/simdutf at b91b70d7).

Checks 7 properties (listed below); the first, an API contract: base64_length_from_binary(n, option) must equal the number of characters binary_to_base64 actually writes.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against simdutf at commit b91b70d7 with 2 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Decode path: binary_length_from_base64 never exceeds maximal_binary_length_from_base64, for arbitrary (mostly invalid) base64 text in char or char16_t ([lines 41-49](source/base64.cpp#L41-L49)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Under loose last-chunk handling, a successful base64_to_binary must report exactly binary_length_from_base64 bytes ([lines 60-67](source/base64.cpp#L60-L67)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- base64_to_binary_safe with a fuzzed output-buffer size: written length <= buffer size (assert); on OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and BASE64_INPUT_REMAINDER the reported input count <= input size (abort); on INVALID_BASE64_CHARACTER the error position < input size (assert) ([lines 103-125](source/base64.cpp#L103-L125)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- base64_length_from_binary(n, option) must equal the number of characters binary_to_base64 actually writes ([lines 184-190](source/base64.cpp#L184-L190)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at lines 103-125 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch simdutf` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.
